items.definition: The overall system through which a country or region produces, exchanges, and manages goods, services, and wealth.
exampleSentences: Turkey's economy expanded at its fastest pace in three years, fueled by strong exports.
A sudden spike in oil prices can ripple through the entire economy.
Economists disagree on how quickly the economy will recover from the recession.

items.definition: The management of money, investments, and credit, especially by governments, companies, or individuals.
exampleSentences: She left law to pursue a career in corporate finance.
The startup struggled to secure finance for its expansion plans.
Public finance decisions made today will shape the national budget for decades.

items.definition: Money that a person, household, or organization regularly receives from work, investments, or other sources.
exampleSentences: Households with a low income spend a larger share of their earnings on food.
Rental properties can provide a steady stream of income.
The tax reform mainly benefits people in the middle-income bracket.

items.definition: A proportion or rate expressed as a fraction of one hundred, commonly used to describe change, share, or comparison.
exampleSentences: Unemployment fell by two percent over the past year.
Only thirty percent of respondents supported the new tax policy.
The company's profits rose ten percent compared with the previous quarter.

items.definition: A distinct area or branch of economic activity, such as manufacturing, agriculture, or services.
exampleSentences: Job growth in the technology sector has outpaced the rest of the economy.
The government introduced subsidies to support the struggling agricultural sector.
Investors are shifting funds from the energy sector into healthcare.

items.definition: A legally binding agreement between two or more parties that sets out specific obligations and terms.
exampleSentences: The two companies signed a five-year supply contract worth millions of dollars.
Her contract includes a clause preventing her from joining a rival firm.
The firm was awarded the government contract after a competitive tender.

items.definition: A good or service produced in one country and sold to buyers in another.
exampleSentences: Machinery and textiles remain the country's largest exports.
The weaker currency made exports more competitive on world markets.
The government offered tax incentives to firms that increased their exports.

items.definition: To supply goods, products, or resources to different people, places, or outlets.
exampleSentences: The company distributes its products to retailers across Europe through a single warehouse.
Profits were distributed among shareholders at the end of the fiscal year.
Aid agencies struggled to distribute supplies to remote areas after the flood.

items.definition: Physical or mental work, especially the workforce considered as a whole in relation to production and employment.
exampleSentences: Rising wages have pushed many manufacturers to look for cheaper labour abroad.
The construction industry depends heavily on skilled labour.
Automation has reduced the demand for manual labour in factories.

items.definition: A course of action or set of principles adopted by a government, institution, or company to guide decisions.
exampleSentences: The central bank tightened monetary policy to curb inflation.
Under the new return policy, customers have thirty days to request a refund.
Critics argue the policy favours large corporations over small businesses.

items.definition: Of great importance, size, or seriousness, especially when contrasted with something smaller or less significant.
exampleSentences: The merger created one of the major players in the airline industry.
There was a major shift in consumer spending after the price hikes.
Losing its biggest client was a major setback for the firm.

items.definition: The place, person, or thing from which something originates or is obtained.
exampleSentences: Tourism is the country's main source of foreign currency.
The report failed to disclose the source of its funding.
Renewable energy is becoming an increasingly important source of power.

items.definition: An advantage, profit, or positive outcome gained from something, or a payment provided to support someone.
exampleSentences: Employees at the firm receive health insurance as part of their benefits package.
The tax cut is expected to benefit small businesses the most.
Analysts questioned whether the merger would truly benefit shareholders.

items.definition: One of several elements or circumstances that contributes to a particular result or decision.
exampleSentences: Rising fuel costs were a major factor behind the airline's losses.
When choosing a supplier, price is rarely the only factor considered.
Weather conditions can be a decisive factor in agricultural output.

items.definition: The particular purpose, role, or activity that something is designed or expected to perform.
exampleSentences: The finance department's main function is to manage the company's cash flow.
This software's core function is to automate payroll processing.
As inflation rises, the function of the central bank becomes more critical.

items.definition: To successfully reach a goal or produce a desired result, usually through effort or skill.
exampleSentences: The company achieved record profits despite the economic downturn.
It took the team five years to achieve full compliance with the new regulations.
Few startups achieve profitability within their first year.

items.definition: To obtain or gain possession of something, often through purchase, effort, or a formal process.
exampleSentences: The tech giant acquired its smaller rival for two billion dollars.
New employees are expected to acquire the necessary skills within their first month.
The firm acquired a majority stake in the local distributor.

items.definition: A payment made to someone based on the value of sales or business they generate, or an official body assigned a specific task.
exampleSentences: Real estate agents typically earn a commission of a few percent on each sale.
The government set up a commission to investigate the banking scandal.
Sales staff are motivated by commission rather than a fixed salary.

items.definition: To use up a resource, or to buy and make use of goods and services.
exampleSentences: Heavy industry consumes a significant share of the country's electricity.
Households are consuming less as prices continue to rise.
The factory's new machines consume far less fuel than the old ones.

items.definition: The ability to borrow money or obtain goods on the understanding that payment will follow later, or an amount added to an account.
exampleSentences: Small businesses often rely on bank credit to manage cash flow.
Her credit rating improved after she paid off her outstanding loans.
The supplier agreed to extend credit for another thirty days.

items.definition: To commit money, time, or resources into something with the expectation of future profit or benefit.
exampleSentences: The firm plans to invest heavily in renewable energy over the next decade.
Many young professionals are choosing to invest in the stock market rather than save cash.
Investing in staff training often pays off in higher productivity.

items.definition: To buy something, or the act of buying, typically used in more formal or written contexts than 'buy.'
exampleSentences: The company purchased new equipment to modernize its production line.
Customers who purchase in bulk receive a discount.
The museum's latest purchase was a rare eighteenth-century painting.

items.definition: An asset, material, or supply that can be used to achieve a goal or support an activity.
exampleSentences: The country's natural resources include oil, gas, and minerals.
Managers must allocate limited resources across competing projects.
Human resources are often a company's most valuable asset.

items.definition: A carefully devised plan of action designed to achieve a long-term goal.
exampleSentences: The board approved a new marketing strategy aimed at younger consumers.
Without a clear pricing strategy, the company struggled to compete.
Analysts questioned whether the firm's expansion strategy was too risky.

items.definition: A method of gathering information or opinions from a sample of people, or a general examination of a situation.
exampleSentences: A recent survey found that most employees prefer flexible working hours.
The firm conducted a customer satisfaction survey after the product launch.
Economists rely on business surveys to gauge confidence in the sector.

items.definition: To move something, such as money, staff, or ownership, from one place, account, or person to another.
exampleSentences: The bank transferred the funds to the wrong account by mistake.
She was transferred to the company's Istanbul office after her promotion.
Ownership of the property will transfer once the final payment is made.

items.definition: To manage and oversee the operations, organization, or affairs of a company, institution, or system.
exampleSentences: A separate department administrates employee pension funds.
The new software helps administrate payroll for over a thousand staff.
It takes a dedicated team to administrate such a complex supply chain.

items.definition: A significant effect or influence that one thing has on another, often used in evaluating outcomes or consequences.
exampleSentences: The new tariffs had a severe impact on small exporters.
Researchers are studying the long-term impact of automation on employment.
The marketing campaign made little impact on overall sales.

items.definition: To obtain or guarantee something, often after effort or negotiation, or to make something safe and protected.
exampleSentences: The company secured a major contract with a European retailer.
Investors want assurances that their deposits are secure.
She secured funding for her startup after months of pitching to investors.

items.definition: A single article, product, or point listed or considered separately within a larger set.
exampleSentences: The store had to discount several items that failed to sell before the holidays.
Salary was the first item on the agenda at the negotiation meeting.
Each item on the invoice must match the delivery receipt.
